subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add an enforceable browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what URL classes and coverage guarantees should it own?
rationale: This request adds a security-sensitive public config surface that current browser SSRF hostname allowlists do not define, and automation should not choose whether it is a hard egress-control boundary, an advisory bot-block hint surface, or part of broader egress policy.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific block/warn semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and focused tests against that contract.

options.title: Fold Into Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Make the broader egress-firewall work own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers redirects, subframes, downloads, proxy routing, and warnlist behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable browser denylist and surface best-effort known bot-block warnings that do not claim to prevent network access.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific block/warn semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and focused tests against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest semantic history across browser SSRF defaults, navigation guard unification, and browser policy refactors that this decision would extend.
